generator.params.bud_area.note: The leaf area its `bud` look draws on an organ 1 m long (plantc's shading-area test), so it shades with what it shows: the bud is now its flower closed, where before it drew the fruit ovoid.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Castilleja hispida: stems 20 cm to 40 cm tall.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a hairy herb of a few stems topped by spikes of scarlet, lobed bracts that hide the small greenish flowers. Each stem ends in one spike drawn as a cluster (flowers 1, flower_size 0.09 within the 3 cm to 15 cm the species states; its look's inflorescence 16 flowers, each a third of its length), now that Orobanchaceae's flowers are mostly in spikes; before, the stem bore 16 single flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.45 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dull green leaves; scarlet bracts. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): a two-lipped tube of five joined petals, five sepals, four stamens and a superior pistil of two carpels, in the scarlet of its bracts (the bracts themselves are not drawn), from the characters of Orobanchaceae by the rules at the flowering plants.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

generator.params.bud_spacing.note: The bracts and buds above the open flowers pack into a dense head at the top of the spike, about a third of the open flowers' spacing apart by eye (flowering photographs, observations 338448297, 5589350, 1585541, 217223222, 269885666, 208431319, 211316657, 397951847): a bud's internode as a share of a flower's, judged by eye.
